title: Numbers That Refuse to Split
question: What makes a number prime, and why do primes matter?
hook: Some numbers cannot be arranged into any rectangle of dots, and everything else is built from them.
idea: Primes cannot be broken into smaller factors, and every other whole number above 1 is built from them.

beats.prompt: You try to arrange a number of dots into a grid more than one dot wide and more than one high, and every attempt fails. What kind of number is it?

choices.label: Composite
choices.feedback: Composite numbers are the ones that do form such a grid.

choices.label: Even
choices.feedback: Even numbers above 2 can always be split, so they fail to match this.

beats.explain: A number is prime if its dots cannot be arranged into a rectangle more than one dot wide and high.

beats.prompt: Sort each number from 2 to 6 into its group
beats.explain: 2, 3 and 5 have no divisors besides 1 and themselves, while 4 = 2 × 2 and 6 = 2 × 3.

beats.prompt: Match each term to its meaning
pairs: Every number above 1 is prime or a product of primes, unique up to order
beats.explain: Each term describes how numbers above 1 either resist splitting or are built from primes.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: Any even number n above 2 can be written as 2 × n/2.
So no even number above 2 can be prime.
That means every prime number is odd.
So the smallest prime must be an odd number.
beats.explain: The number 2 is prime and even; every prime other than 2 is odd.
